summary_paragraph: A woman with ESRD on hemodialysis via a right femoral tunneled catheter and advanced HIV/AIDS on HAART presented with progressive right leg swelling and pain shortly after catheter placement. Lower-extremity ultrasound showed no DVT, and CT pelvis demonstrated marked edema but limited assessment for thrombus around the catheter because it occupied most of the right external iliac vein; she was treated for presumed catheter-associated DVT with a heparin infusion bridged to warfarin until therapeutic INR, with swelling resolving after in-hospital dialysis and by discharge. During the admission she developed right-eye conjunctivitis with periorbital swelling and morning purulence; Ophthalmology started polymyxin/bacitracin ointment and a 7-day course of valacyclovir given prior herpes ophthalmicus, and HSV/VZV testing from a lesion was negative with near-complete symptom resolution. Chest discomfort and odynophagia were felt most consistent with esophagitis and resolved after completing a 14-day fluconazole course. She continued scheduled hemodialysis, EPO for anemia of CKD, and HIV therapy with opportunistic infection prophylaxis, and was discharged home with services, warfarin with INR monitoring arranged through dialysis, and completion of eye medications.
problems: Presumed catheter-associated deep venous thrombosis/right lower extremity edema treated with heparin bridge to warfarin
End-stage renal disease on hemodialysis via right femoral tunneled catheter; dialysis access complication
Conjunctivitis/periorbital swelling treated with polymyxin/bacitracin ointment and valacyclovir; HSV/VZV testing negative
Advanced HIV/AIDS on HAART with opportunistic infection prophylaxis
Chest discomfort/odynophagia felt due to esophagitis; completed fluconazole
Anemia of chronic kidney disease treated with EPO during hemodialysis
Secondary hyperparathyroidism; cinacalcet dose reduced and phosphate binder continued
Paroxysmal atrial fibrillation (history; anticoagulation addressed with warfarin for presumed DVT)
Hyperkalemia on admission without EKG changes, improved with dialysis
